items.raw: In male Sprague-Dawley rats with surgically induced partial bladder outlet obstruction, Shirazi et al. gave pentoxifylline 100 mg/kg/day by oral gavage for four weeks after obstruction induction, associated with higher electrically evoked isolated-detrusor-strip tension than water controls (approximately 4.0 ± 1.0 versus 1.8 ± 0.4 g per 100 mg tissue; reported P=0.023). items.raw: Shirazi 2015: in male Sprague-Dawley rats with partial bladder outlet obstruction, pentoxifylline 100 mg/kg/day by oral gavage for four weeks, begun after obstruction induction, produced no significant improvement in maximum carbachol-induced detrusor-strip contractile tension versus water-treated obstructed controls (20 animals per group; all completed). Treatment addressed established obstruction, not prevention; this is a functional contractility null.

items.raw: Rademakers et al.'s review (rademakers2016.pdf.md, Preoperative characterization; Figure 1) reports a retrospective urodynamic analysis attributed to Oelke et al. of 786 treatment-naïve men ≥40 with LUTS: median BCI rose with obstruction grade from 73 (Schäfer 0) to 188 (grade 6), median Wmax from 9.6 to 23 W/m². The review suggests thresholds BCI<100 and Wmax<7 be grade-adjusted—cross-sectional association, not within-man change.

items.raw: Rademakers et al. (rademakers2016.pdf.md), a narrative review, report that Oelke developed the Hannover–Maastricht nomogram from urodynamic data of 822 treatment-naïve men aged ≥40 with LUTS/BPO. It plots bladder-outlet-obstruction index against maximum Watts factor to classify outlet resistance and detrusor contractility simultaneously; values below the 25th-percentile line indicate detrusor underactivity relative to outlet resistance, including when obstruction coexists. Validation remained ongoing.

items.raw: He et al. retrospectively studied 21 men with nonbacterial chronic prostatitis and dysfunctional voiding (2007-2009), selected after antibiotics and alpha-blockers over six months gave poor effects. Diagnostic criteria required no neurological abnormality plus transient, intermittent external-sphincter closure during voiding on EMG and fluoroscopic cysto-urethrography, with raised external-sphincter EMG activity without abdominal-pressure increase (he2010.pdf.md, Patients and Methods).

items.raw: He et al. (he2010.pdf.md, PATIENTS AND METHODS; RESULTS, TABLE 1) report a retrospective, uncontrolled series of 21 men with nonbacterial chronic prostatitis and dysfunctional voiding whose Qmax rose 8.2 (SD 4.1) to 15.1 (SD 7.3) mL/s after ~10 weeks of relaxation/coordination biofeedback, not strengthening (P<0.05); antibiotics, α-blockers, anticholinergics suspended. Lacking a placebo control, this within-cohort change isn't a controlled effect.

items.raw: Shirazi et al. (Comparison-between-combination-of-tamsulosin-and-Pentoxifylline-versus-tamsulosin-alone-in.pdf.md): single-center randomized double-blind trial, 30 men per arm (all analyzed) with BPH/LUTS, giving pentoxifylline 400 mg every eight hours plus tamsulosin 0.4 mg/day or placebo plus tamsulosin, 12 weeks. Post-void residual fell more with combination (−32.93±16.33 versus −13.17±9.23 mL; p<.001), but baseline residual differed (77.27 versus 50.37 mL; p=.18). Reported values, not validated or baseline-equivalent.

Parent-PTX plasma Tpeak was 1.64 ± 0.92 versus 3.89 ± 1.90 h (NYHA II, n=11; III/IV, n=9; P=.0077); Cmax 719 ± 403 versus 833 ± 524 ng/mL (NS), mean ± SD. Plasma values only—no tissue, unbound, metabolite or half-life—not urinary-benefit timing.

items.raw: Roberts et al. report that pentoxifylline 5 μmol/L added to healthy volunteers' whole blood (30-minute preincubation, 37°C) reduced FMLP-stimulated neutrophil intracellular oxidant (DCF hydrogen-peroxide) production to 76 ± 5% of the PTX-free response (mean ± SE; n=10; p<0.025). This added, parent-drug concentration—not plasma or metabolite exposure—is ex vivo and does not establish a bladder response (roberts1993.pdf.md).

items.raw: Delanian et al. 2003, single-center randomized double-blind placebo-controlled 2×2 factorial trial in women with superficial radiation-induced fibrosis >6 months after breast radiotherapy (24 eligible, 22 with 6-month data). Combination pentoxifylline 800 mg/day plus vitamin E 1000 U/day gave −60.2% versus double-placebo −42.6% surface-area change (P=.038, Wilcoxon). Two-way ANOVA found no significant main effects, only a PTX×vitamin-E interaction trend (P=.09).

items.raw: Delanian et al.'s follow-up of women with superficial breast radiation-induced fibrosis on pentoxifylline 800 mg/day plus vitamin E 1,000 U/day found that, after stopping, fibrosis surface area rebounded more after short (6-12-month) treatment than long (24-48-month) treatment: 40%/year (95% CI 24-56) versus 8.5%/year (95% CI 1-16); P=.0012. Duration was not randomized; follow-up lasted two years (delanian2005.pdf.md).

items.raw: Kassar et al.'s systematic review/meta-analysis of four depression RCTs (318 participants) found no significant difference in all-cause discontinuation between pentoxifylline and placebo: 14/159 versus 16/159; pooled RR 0.88 (95% CI 0.45-1.74; P=0.72). items.raw: In Parker et al.'s randomized, investigator-blinded porcine haemorrhage-plus-E.-coli-peritonitis experiment (female Large White pigs; n=5 per group), pentoxifylline plus colloid (20 mg/kg bolus, then 20 mg/kg over 60 minutes) gave lower median 2-hour MAP than colloid-plus-saline placebo: 62(10) versus 92(10) mmHg (P<0.01); by 6 hours groups did not differ. items.raw: In Ridings et al.'s nonrandomized controlled porcine sepsis experiment (ridings1994.pdf.md, COMMENT), intravenous pentoxifylline (20 mg/kg bolus, 6 mg/kg/h) begun two hours after Pseudomonas infusion (established, uncorrected shock) was followed by fatal hypotension within one hour in 2/4 animals; two survivors resembled 1-hour-treated protection (data not shown). Authors attributed deaths to pentoxifylline but said n=4 precluded statistics; untransferable to bladder dysfunction.

items.raw: Wystrychowski et al. (wystrychowski2014.pdf.md, Table 1; RESULTS) randomized 58 male Sprague-Dawley rats; after right nephrectomy, solitary left pedicle was clamped 45 minutes. Subcutaneous pentoxifylline 100 mg/kg versus saline improved 48-hour creatinine clearance only when given 60 minutes before ischemia (10/arm; P<.001), not 1 minute into ischemia or 60 minutes post-release. These within-timing acute-model results don't transfer to chronic bladder disease.

items.raw: FitzGerald et al. (fitzgerald2009.pdf.md), a randomized multicenter feasibility trial (47 total), report the male CP/CPPS subgroup (11 assigned myofascial PT, 10 global massage; 11 versus 9 at week 12). Preliminary; uroflow/residual and prior pelvic-floor-treatment history not reported.

items.raw: Raison et al. 2013, 12-week double-blind placebo-controlled randomized trial in 60 medically stable treatment-resistant-depression outpatients: infliximab (5 mg/kg intravenously at baseline, weeks 2 and 6; n=30) versus placebo (n=30) produced no statistically significant overall difference in 17-item HAM-D change over time (intention-to-treat mixed-effects, t58=0.10, P=.92). Nonsignificant, not proof of no benefit; this is infliximab for depression.

items.raw: Roerink et al.'s cross-sectional matched case-control study found that 17 patients in long-term remission of Cushing's syndrome had lower mean peak oxygen uptake during incremental bicycle exercise than 17 individually matched healthy controls: 28.0 ± 7.0 versus 34.8 ± 7.9 mL O2/kg/min (mean ± SD; P<0.01). Remission exceeded four years (median 11.3, range 4-28) (roerink2019.pdf.md).

items.raw: Shah et al. (shah2016.pdf.md, Regression Analysis; Discussion) studied 31 Cushing's-disease patients during active disease and after endocrine remission. Adjusted for age, gender, BMI, visceral/subcutaneous/total adipose masses, hepatic and inter-muscular fat did not predict plasma IL-6 or IL-1β at either visit; cytokines were not associated with insulin resistance. These are nonassociations, not causal exclusion; which cytokines stayed elevated isn't stated here.

items.raw: Bortnick and colleagues' review states that phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors are contraindicated in patients taking nitrates, because they might potentiate nitrates' effect and cause life-threatening hypotension. This is class-level contraindication guidance with a proposed interaction rationale, not a quantified, observed adverse-event rate (bortnick2019.pdf.md, Phosphodiesterase Inhibitors).

items.raw: Vale et al. (vale2019.pdf.md, §3.1.4 Bladder outlet obstruction), a review, reports that in mice with bladder outlet obstruction, daily 17-DMAG (described as pharmacological HIF-pathway inhibition) improved BOO-induced morphology, suppressed HIF target-gene upregulation, and seemed to improve stimulated contractility (attributed to Iguchi, Malykhina, Wilcox 2016, ref 55). This is review-level proposed-mechanism description, not demonstrated psychogenic causation, a prevalence estimate, or treatment-response data.

items.raw: Spinas 1991, randomized study of 20 healthy men: endotoxin alone (n=7), endotoxin plus oral ibuprofen (800 mg 120 minutes before, 800 mg immediately before; n=6), or saline (n=7). items.raw: Glazener et al. 2011, UK randomized TURP trial: 442 men with incontinence six weeks post-surgery were offered four one-to-one PFMT (plus bladder training) sessions (n=220) or standard care (n=222). At 12 months, self-reported any incontinence (ICIQ-UI SF) was 126/194 (65%) versus 125/203 (62%); adjusted intention-to-treat risk ratio 1.06 (95% CI 0.91–1.23; p=0.47)—no significant benefit. Post-surgical leakage, not difficult emptying.
